Thiazide diuretics are commonly used in nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (p.2179) and NSAIDs may also be employed; both result in an overall decrease in urine produc- tion. Hydrochlorothiazide with amiloride has been reported to be at least as effective as hydrochlorothiazide plus indometacin in 5 patients.1 In addition, amiloride obviated the need for potassium supplements. Hydrochlorothiazide with amiloride was also ef- fective and well tolerated in a group of 4 children with nephro- genic diabetes insipidus who were treated for up to 5 years.2 1.
